summary: Elizabeth J. Harris is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of Kelaniya and earned her doctorate from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under Ananda W. P. Guruge and Y. Karunadasa (~1988–1993), later holding a post at the University of Birmingham (~2017).
Elizabeth Mills is an Indologist who completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 2011. Attested in 2020, she taught Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto.

Elizabeth Morrison works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She studied under Bernard Faure, Carl Bielefeldt, Ellen Neskar, Janet Gyatso, and Susan Niditch, and held posts at Amherst College (1998–1999) and Middlebury College (attested 2008).

Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Paul Groner, and Geshe Wangyal, and served as co-director at the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).
Elke Rogersdotter is an archaeologist and Indologist. Attested in 2006, she completed her PhD at Umeå University under Thomas B. Larsson, Bozena Werbart, Karin Viklund, and P. Ajithprasad.
Ellen M. Raven is an Indologist and archaeologist who held posts at Leiden University, attested in 2003 and on the Editorial Board in 2018.
Elliot M. Stern is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He pursued his doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania, where he was a Ph.D. candidate until 1988 and earned his Ph.D. by 1998.

Elliot Sperling (1951–2017) was a Tibetologist and historian. He studied at Queens College (~1969–1973) and earned his PhD at Indiana University (~1976–1983) under Helmut Hoffmann and Lynn A. Struve, later serving on the faculties of Harvard University and Indiana University (~1987–2015).

Ellison Banks Findly is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied under Fred Pfeil (attested 2000) and held posts at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College (attested 1989).
Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetologist who held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2018).

Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He held posts as Pandit at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library, at the Sanskrit Pathashala in Vadtal (attested 1937), and at Baroda College (attested 1939).

Emi Matsushita (b. 1970) studied at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and earned an MA from Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She held positions with the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education (1994–1996) and Ohio State University (1999–2001).

Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) was a linguist who studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1821–1825). He held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1830–1860) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1860–1874).

Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Kiel. He held positions at Humboldt University of Berlin (1896–1908), the University of Kiel (~1909–1920), and the University of Göttingen (~1920–1935).

Emilio Teza (1831–1912) was an Italian linguist and Indologist who studied under Anton Boller (~1851–1854). He held posts at the University of Bologna (~1860–1861), the University of Pisa (~1861–1887), and the University of Padua (~1887–1911).

Emily T. Yeh (b. 1971) is a Tibetologist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1993, 1995) and the University of California, Berkeley (2003). She held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder (~2003).

Emmie te Nijenhuis (b. 1931) is an Indologist who studied at the Utrecht School of the Arts and completed her PhD at Utrecht University (~1961–1970). She later held a post at the University of Amsterdam.

Enamul Haque (1937–2022) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka and the University of Oxford (~1970–1973). He held a post at the Bangladesh National Museum (~1962–1991).

Encho Tamura (1917–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, archaeology, and Japanology. Educated at Kyoto University and Kyushu University (-1941), he held posts at Kyushu University (~1963–2013), Shitennoji University (attested 1976), Kumamoto University (~1980–1983), Kyushu Historical Museum (~1983), and Fukuoka Prefectural Human Rights Center.

Endo Asai (1927–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies who graduated from the University of Tokyo in 1949. He held posts at Rissho University (~1969–1997), Minobusan University (~1999–2003), and Nihon Fukushi University.
